pr_title: networkd: fix DHCP on InfiniBand interfaces
pr_body:
With these patches applied, networkd is successfully able to get an address from a DHCP server on an IPoIB interface.

For one, networkd-dhcp4.c simply didn't pass on the actual interface type, and instead had it hardcoded to ARPHRD_ETHER.

On top of that, the dhcp handling code did not handle the MAC address entirely correct.
It insisted on its size in dhcp_network_bind_raw_socket, where it didn't even use it.

And in sd_dhcp_client_set_mac it also insists on it being the full 20 bytes, even though the systemd network code passes the "emulated" standard MAC address. Which for everything the DHCP client uses it for, is perfectly fine to use.

Fixes #17322.
pr_comments:
There's two things that are potentially still missing for full proper support.
One is reading and passing on the actual full 20 byte MAC address. Or at least the last 8 bytes of it.
For Client-ID generation only the last 8 bytes of that need to be passed on. Right now it will not generate the correct ClientID expected by a DHCP server which is assigning static leases.

The other is reading the broadcast address from the device somehow.
The default broadcast address built into the code right now is not always correct, and the actual one needs to be fetched from the device.

Both of these changes appear to require larger changes to the entire netlink interface, so I'm omitting them here.
Might take a look at them at some later point.

Turns out the netlink stuff is fine, just cannot use the _ether functions to get the addresses.
So adding the full hw and bcast addresses to the Link struct is simple enough.

Passing in the actual broadcast address required some slightly wider changes, but nothing too crazy luckily.
With those additional changes DHCP now works even on interfaces which use a non-default broadcast address.
MAC-Based ClientID now also works correctly and matches what other DHCP clients send, instead of the truncated, always identical, first 6 byte of the Interface MAC.

What probably still does not work, because it uses the hardcoded 6 byte Ether-MAC-Struct, is DAD. Changing that seems like a much bigger endevaour.

I can squash this down to one if that's preferred.
My idea with this split was to improve bisectability.

idea:

For IPv4/IPv6 addresses we added `union in_addr_union` as a type that can store either an ipv4 or an ipv6 address. Maybe we should take inspiration from that, and least in our internal code add `union hw_addr` that then consist of  a `struct ether_addr` or a `uint8_t infiniband[INFINIBAND_ALEN]` as alternatives (and whatever other hw addresses sooner or later for sure will pop up). 

The sd-dhcp API should probably stick to generic `uint8_t* hw_addr` style parameters, but at least the internal code would become a lot easier if we could just use a union that is appropriately sized.

Yes, that would definitely be the cleaner solution.
The struct + union would also need a way to hold the length of the address though, unless you always want to infer that from the interface type.

Added a union and struct, based on how it's done for in_addr_union/data and started using it for the Link struct.
Obviously there's _a lot_ of places where a 6 byte ethernet mac is a hardcoded expectation. For those I just pass it as is, which will behave like it behaves right now.
In the future, those places and functions can be gradually migrated to be aware of arbitrarily sized hardware addresses.

Edit: Not sure how to deal with the test failure.
Is that not the right header to put it?
Changed it to internal functions now, making it more public is something that can be decided and done later on and is not really in the scope of fixing DHCP for IB anyway.

LGTM, though I cannot test this, as I do not have infiniband interfaces. Maybe, we need to update `sd_xxx_set_mac()` for other engines, e.g., DHCP6 client. But let's do that later.

@poettering What do you think the above comment https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/17444#discussion_r511927542?

issue_context.title: networkd: DHCP on InfiniBand(IPoIB) interface does not work
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
 > 246

**Used distribution**
 > Gentoo

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
 > 5.4.70

**CPU architecture issue was seen on**
 > amd64

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**

I was expecting networkd with DHCP=yes on an IB interface to successfully request an IP from a DHCP Server.
The DHCP server (Mellanox-Patched ISC DHCPd) is working fine for PXE boot and via dhclient.

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**

The DHCP server never sees any kind of request from the machine running the networkd DHCP client.
Additionally, when enabling debug logging in networkd, I can see it starting the "DHCP CLIENT", but after that it only ever logs about IPv6 RA. No sign of it actually sending any DHCP request(s).

**Steps to reproduce the problem**

Run networkd on any machine with an IPoIB interface, with the most basic DHCP=yes networkd config for the respective interface.
The used IB card is a ConnectX-4 VPI running with the in-kernel mlx5 driver with IPoIB enhancements enabled in my case.
comments: We don't have this interface. Can you please capture packets on that interface with networkd debug logs.

tcpdump does not show any (IPv4) traffic on the interface on port 67 or 68 whatsoever. (Or on any port really)
Log of networkd: https://gist.github.com/BtbN/4cfbab09113c95aba8fcbc9f29ad4bb8

I manually assigned an address to the interface at some point near the end, in order to access the log.

Thank for the logs
```

Oct 12 21:24:10 node01 systemd-networkd[5436]: DHCP CLIENT (0x983477a3): STARTED on ifindex 4
```

right no packets (not even discoverer)  can be seen .  Not sure why packets are not passing throw.  Does even any ipv4 packets passed via this interface
No, if I run an unconditional tcpdump alongside a networkd restart, all it shows are IPv6 RA things. Nothing IPv4.

What I want to say is, we need to figure why no IPv4 packets not going via this interface. If no IPv4 packets throw then we can't talk to server and no IPv4 DHCP address. I think this is not about networkd rather why IPv4 traffic not going throw.

As a note about DHCP for IPoIB: It's a bit different from regular DHCP. For the ISC DHCP client and server, you need to apply a Patch that originates from Mellanox to add support(https://src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/dhcp/blob/master/f/0014-IPoIB-support-660681.patch).
However, looking at the networkd dhcp code, it at least is aware of some specialties surrounding IB interfaces: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/master/src/libsystemd-network/dhcp-network.c#L118
Well I am asking about just any IPv4 traffic. Can you capture any ?

If I manually assign an IPv4 address to the interface it works fine and the traffic does show up in tcpdump.
However networkds DHCP client does not send any IPv4 traffic on the interface at all, and also does not log about trying to.
Not sure what to do about that.
The .network file is quite literally just

```
[Match]
Name=ibp1s0

[Network]
DHCP=ipv4
```

To mimic a bit more closely to how dhclient seems to handle the DHCP situation on IPoIB, I changed the config to:

```
[Match]
Name=ibp1s0

[Network]
DHCP=ipv4
RequestBroadcast=yes
ClientIdentifier=mac
```

But no dice, still not a single DHCP packet to be seen on tcpdump.

i don't know anything about InfiniBand, but does broadcasting actually work? if not i think it wont work using a standard DHCP client. i.e. the client would need to know where to send packets to instead of a broadcast address...

It works, yes.
See what needs changed in dhclient for it to work: https://src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/dhcp/blob/master/f/0014-IPoIB-support-660681.patch

The primary two change to the client are `ip->client->config->bootp_broadcast_always = 1;` and enforcing a client-id to be set, for the lack of a MAC-Address on those broadcasts.

Both of these things are already present in networkd, so there must be some other issue somewhere, that prevents networkd from operating properly.

I traced this down a bit more by adding debug prints into the code.
In sd-dhcp-client.c, it calls client_send_discover, which then calls dhcp_client_send_raw.
dhcp_client_send_raw returns -22, which means EINVAL.
Which originates from sendto() in dhcp_network_send_raw_socket() in dhcp-network.c.

Did not get to investigate why exactly it fails to send.

Edit: After some further investigation, it seems like in https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/master/src/network/networkd-dhcp4.c
The arp_type is just hardcoded to ARPHRD_ETHER in multiple places.

review_comments: why this? shouldn't the size be clear from context?

I think it's worth having the size there still, even if purely as a sanity check.
There's a couple places that sanity-check the address length against the interface type already, so if that length then gets derived from the iftype initially, that becomes kinda pointless.

It also simplifies the code a bit, specially when the hw_addr is to be used in places that right now use the iftype.

Hmm, I agree with the suggestion by @poettering. The functions `netlink_message_read_in_addr_union()` or `_append_` take family `AF_INET` or `AF_INET6`. So, similarly, the new functions should take iftype.

I'm really not sure about that.
Doing it that way would add a lot of complexity and logic in places that don't otherwise need it.
See for example the print functions I just added and their example usage in the networkctl status output.
That code right now does not need to care about the iftype, but if it would, it would need changed every time a new iftype gets supported.

I'm also somewhat afraid that changing it to behave like it does for in_addr_union, where the family, or in this case iftype, is passed along everywhere causes a chain of regressions where formally implicitly supported interface types that behave like ethernet (I see references to CAN, PPP, WiFi-Devices and probably some tunnel devices) will then cause assertions because it's neither ETHER nor INFINIBAND, and compiling the full list everywhere seems way worse than just carrying along the size.
OK. After grepping kernel codes, the length of `IFLA_ADDRESS` may have variety of length. I changed my mind. Let's keep this as is at least now.
can you extend the commit msg here? i.e. move the explanatory stuff from the PR description into the commit descriptions please? (applies here and to the other commits a bit, too)
hmm, binding to the broadcast addr? can you explain?

It's a raw/packet socket, and the broadcast address in this case is the hardware broadcast address (6 bytes of 0xFF in case of ethernet, something rather complex and not set in stone in the case of IB).
The initial discover is broadcasted out via this socket. Once the DHCP server is known normal UDP unicast is used.
